about:
Arkansas Steel Associates, LLC (ASA) was founded in 1989 as a joint venture between Yamato Kogyo and Sumitomo Corporation. The plant sits on 300 acres in Newport, Arkansas, in the northeastern part of the state.

ASA manufactures merchant bar quality (MBQ) billets, hot-rolled flat bars, and double-shoulder railroad tie plates. The facility produces tie plates to A.R.E.M.A. and customer specifications, with standard offerings covering rail sizes from 115RE to 140RE. Flat bars are produced in a variety of cross sections and lengths, all meeting Buy America requirements.

The company serves the railroad industry, supplying tie plates to customers that range from small contractors to Class 1 railroads across North America. Its products are also used in construction projects requiring domestically sourced steel.

ASA maintains ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 14001:2015 certifications, reflecting a focus on quality management and environmental performance. The company has also published a decarbonization plan targeting zero Scope 2 emissions for its electric furnaces.

Arkansas Truck Center operates from Alma, Arkansas, as a family-owned business specializing in heavy-duty truck parts and recovery services. The company maintains over 30 acres of late-model truck inventory and a 13,000-square-foot warehouse stocked with new, used, and remanufactured components for Peterbilt and Freightliner models.

The center functions as a parts distributor and wrecker service provider, offering worldwide shipping for local pickup or delivery. Its inventory spans new, used, and remanufactured parts, and the company also purchases trucks coast to coast for resale, export, scrap, or parts dismantling. The wrecker recovery service supports heavy-duty equipment retrieval.

Customers include trucking fleets, owner-operators, and repair shops needing Peterbilt and Freightliner components, as well as those requiring heavy-duty recovery. The business serves both domestic and international buyers through its shipping program.

The company emphasizes its family-owned heritage and commitment to modern equipment and trained personnel as differentiators in a market where equipment has grown more sophisticated.

old_description: We are a family owned and operated business. We have been at our current location since 1964. Our business was founded by my father Fred Philippus. I have been involved with the company since 1965. My wife and I have owned the company since 1985.
about:
Arrow Sheet Metal Works, Inc. operates from Tampa, Florida, where it has been located since 1964. The business was founded in 1952 by Fred Philippus and remains family-owned; his son Bob Philippus and his wife have held ownership since 1985. Bob, who has been involved since 1965, serves as vice president.

The company provides custom sheet metal fabrication, working with stainless steel, aluminum, steel, galvanized steel, brass, and copper. Its shop performs welding, grinding, polishing, shearing, and bending of materials up to 1/2 inch thick, as well as pipe bending up to 2 inches in diameter. Typical output includes countertops, handrails, brackets, platforms, frames, stands, kitchen hood shells, shelving, racks, panels, cabinets, truck boxes, light brackets, and transition fittings. Field installation and portable welding services are also offered, and local delivery is handled with company-owned pickup trucks and a flatbed.

Arrow serves both commercial and residential customers throughout the Tampa Bay area. Named accounts include Tampa Electric Company, Busch Gardens/SeaWorld, Southern Wine and Spirits, Tampa International Airport, Outback Steakhouse, McDonald's, Hanna Bartoletta Homes, Hillsborough County, and the City of Tampa, alongside numerous residential clients.

The firm emphasizes that no job is too big or too small, building custom pieces that cannot be purchased off the shelf. Its founding premise was to provide specialized fabrication for projects that standard hardware stores cannot supply.

about:
Atlas Metal Works LLC operates from South Windsor, Connecticut, as a CT DAS Certified Small Business Enterprise. The company runs a custom metal fabrication house serving the commercial market, though its founding year and founders are not publicly disclosed.

The shop provides end-to-end fabrication from design through finished parts, including laser cutting, high-definition plasma cutting, shearing, press-brake forming, CNC punching, pipe rolling and bending, polishing, sawing, and multiple welding processes (MIG, TIG, flux-core, spot, stud, and aluminum MIG). Key equipment includes a BLM LS5 12 kW plate laser cutting 5-by-10-foot plates up to one inch thick, a Vectis UR20 cobot welder with 48-inch reach, two AccurPress brakes (320-ton by 12-foot and 175-ton by 10-foot), an AccurShear with 1/4-inch by 12-foot capacity, a 55-ton Euromac CNC punch, a Timesaver 8-inch stainless polisher, Hypertherm and Thermadyne high-definition plasma systems, and a Marvel 18-inch automated saw. The company also stocks and sells raw sheet, plate, angle, and channel cut to size.

Customers span OEM manufacturers, general contractors, construction firms, and other fabrication houses that need supplemental capacity. Work ranges from commercial and residential projects to industrial applications, with the shop handling everything from gauge sheet to heavy plate in stainless steel, aluminum, carbon steel, galvanized, brass, and copper.

Atlas Metal Works positions itself as a gap-filler for manufacturers lacking in-house shearing, bending, laser cutting, welding, or hole-punching capacity. It accepts customer design files in AutoCAD, FastCAM, or FastSHAPES formats and can also create designs in-house, aiming to deliver accurate parts on schedule for both large and small projects.

about:
Atlas Wire, LLC was founded in 1966 in Itasca, Illinois. The company began as a supplier to the electronic, OEM, and distribution markets and has since expanded to operate a second facility in Tucson, Arizona. Ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The company manufactures PVC, XLPE (cross-linked polyethylene), and nylon insulated electrical lead wires in single and multi-conductor constructions, covering sizes from 4 to 30 AWG. Its capabilities include extrusion, spiral striping, longitudinal line extrusion, twisting, heat bonding, respooling, and custom drum or spool packaging. Atlas Wire has produced over 4,900 distinct wire types across its two plants.

Atlas Wire serves the electronics, automotive, military, appliance, building and fixture, and industrial machinery sectors. Customers include OEMs and distributors that require UL-recognized appliance wire, machine tool wire, low-voltage automotive primary wire and battery cable, military hookup wire, and PVC-insulated building wire.

The company emphasizes a service-oriented approach, citing low minimum order quantities, short production lead times, and a willingness to accommodate special requirements as key differentiators. Its quality system is certified to ISO 9001 and IATF 16949.

Its terminal operations feature a non‑TWIC receiving area and are structured for high‑volume, quick‑turnaround cargo handling.

The company states its mission is to meet or exceed customer expectations every time, backed by ISO 9001 certification and facilities that meet all automotive manufacturer guidelines. AutoPort also emphasizes vehicle decarbonization as part of a shift toward carbon neutrality.

about:
Avatar Natural Foods was founded in 2011 and operates from a 70,000-square-foot facility in Henderson, Nevada. The company grew from the culinary vision of chef Diego Silva, creator of the Eat Pita brand, who set out to make clean, healthy American food affordable and accessible. The business remains privately held and centers its operations around a cluster of sister brands—YaYa's Kitchen, Tuscany Cookies, Eat Pita, Bettr Bowl, and Cali Crumble—each developed in the facility's production and test kitchens.

The company manufactures and distributes a line of gourmet, all-natural food products that span deli salads, Mediterranean dips, grab-and-go meals, baked goods, pita bread, pita chips, frozen entrees, and cookies. In addition to its own brands, Avatar provides private-label manufacturing, co-packing with package design and shipping, wholesale distribution, and e-commerce fulfillment with 24-hour order processing. The plant holds FDA registration, USDA Organic certification, HACCP, and GMP certification, and runs hundreds of SKUs through its production lines.

Avatar serves independent retailers, supermarkets, greengrocers, delicatessens, garden centers, pound shops, cash-and-carry outlets, and expatriate shops across the continental United States. Its customer base spans food-service operators, grocery chains, and online sellers looking for clean-label, preservative-free products.

Silva's founding mission—to replace artificial ingredients with fresh, non-GMO, preservative-free recipes at an affordable price—still drives the operation. The company emphasizes that controlling every step from recipe development to distribution lets it pass cost savings to customers while maintaining a "healthy, premium, and fresh" standard.

about:
Averra Packaging is based in West Valley City, Utah. The company was founded in 2013, though its thermoforming roots trace back to a garage operation started in 1989. Tim Neiman serves as CEO, a team that includes veterans of medical device manufacturing and packaging.

The company designs and manufactures custom sterile packaging for medical devices, as well as consumer packaging. Its 40,000-square-foot facility operates a Class 8 cleanroom and is cGMP compliant, with ISO 13485:2016 and ISO 9001:2015 certifications. Processes include thermoforming, in-house prototyping, bridge tooling for production-equivalent samples, and full-scale production supported by an internal machine shop that builds and maintains tooling. The equipment fleet handles volumes ranging from hundreds of parts to tens of millions annually.

Averra serves medical device manufacturers, healthcare companies, and consumer goods brands. Its healthcare portfolio includes custom trays, lids, and fulfillment services, with the company also acting as manufacturer of record for clients seeking a single point of accountability. Consumer packaging projects focus on shelf-impact design combined with functional performance.

The company emphasizes sustainable practices, reporting that 75 percent of its materials come from recycled content, one million pounds of post-production waste are recycled each year, and 96 percent of its products are recyclable. Averra positions itself as a development partner rather than a vendor, offering manufacturer-of-record capabilities to streamline quality systems and documentation for medical device launches.

Azuma Foods International Inc. USA (AFI) was founded in 1990 and is headquartered in East Rutherford, New Jersey. The business was created to bring traditional Japanese food culture to a global audience by merging it with other culinary traditions.

AFI specializes in the import, processing, and distribution of Japanese-inspired seafood and specialty food products. Its product lines include tobikko (flying fish roe), masago (capelin roe), dry toppings, seaweed salad, calamari salad, and a range of sushi-grade, appetizer, fry-and-grill, and plant-based items. The company operates an in-house laboratory equipped for pathogen testing using PCR thermal cyclers, ELISA assays, and culture methods, and it develops new products through its R&D team. All foreign suppliers must provide HACCP plans and certificates of compliance, and AFI manages allergen control, gluten testing, and FSVP programs.

The company primarily serves the food service industry, supplying restaurants, catering operations, and institutional kitchens with ready-to-use seafood salads, roe products, and plant-based options. Its menu catalog and recipe ideas target chefs and food service buyers looking for Japanese-inspired ingredients.

AFI was founded on the principle of assimilating food cultures, aiming to introduce traditional Japanese flavors to global markets through innovative product development. The company emphasizes rigorous food safety, with HACCP and SQF certifications, third-party audits, and a comprehensive quality management system that covers everything from supplier verification to in-house microbial testing.

Notable installations include a paddle mixer system across four plants for a snack stick producer, a spiral system for a large bacon processor that combined smoking, cooking, and chilling in a continuous line, and a bowl chopper upgrade for a farm-to-retail meat processor.

BSU Electronics operates from Austin, Texas, where it has manufactured printed circuit board assemblies since relocating from its founding location in Ithaca, New York. What began as a PCB assembly shop has grown into a full-service electronics contract manufacturer serving customers from startup phase through global production.

The company provides end-to-end electronics manufacturing including rigid, flex, and rigid‑flex PCB assembly using surface‑mount, through‑hole, and press‑fit processes. Its facility handles box‑build and electromechanical system integration, custom cable and wire harness assembly (including fiber optic, RF, coax, and high‑gauge overmolded designs), conformal coating, and software/firmware programming. Testing capabilities span flying‑probe, 5D X‑ray, 3D automated optical inspection, in‑line solder paste inspection, functional test, boundary scan, ionic contamination, temperature cycling, and high‑potential verification. All work is performed to IPC‑A‑610, IPC J‑STD‑001, and IPC/WHMA‑A‑620 standards with full traceability under ITAR registration.

BSU serves aerospace programs with mission‑critical avionics, communication boards, and aircraft spares; defense customers with manned and unmanned system components; semiconductor equipment builders including wafer‑fabrication platforms; medical technology firms; transportation projects ranging from roller coasters and monorails to autonomous and electric vehicles; energy sector subassemblies for generation, storage, and AI data‑center power; and broader industrial automation, sensor, and instrumentation electronics. Long‑term relationships include a 30‑year safety‑equipment client and multiple multi‑decade aerospace and defense accounts supplying the U.S. government.

The company emphasizes engineer‑led sourcing and design‑for‑X collaboration so that manufacturability issues surface during build rather than qualification. It advertises flexible lead times — under 24‑hour turnaround when components are on hand, three‑day new‑quote response, and one‑day rush for repeat customers — backed by direct, proactive engineering engagement throughout each project.

about:
BTL Liners, based in Prineville, Oregon, traces its roots to 1981 when Ron Perlatti founded Bend Tarp and Liner in Bend. The company began installing pond liners in the mid-1980s and partnered with a Japanese firm to develop the first heavyweight reinforced polyethylene liners. Ownership passed to Perlatti's son Brad and his wife Jan in 1997, and the operation moved to its current 84,000-square-foot facility in Prineville in 2007, adopting the BTL Liners name. In 2021, their daughter Chelsea and her husband Travis Wilcox took over, continuing the third-generation family ownership.

The company manufactures custom geomembrane liners, covers, and tarps from reinforced polyethylene (RPE), reinforced polypropylene (RPP), and low-density polyethylene (LDPE). Its purpose-built fabrication plant houses welding and prefabrication equipment capable of producing single panels up to 150,000 square feet. A team of 20-plus handles design, fabrication, and installation support offered worldwide, either on-site or remotely.

BTL serves agriculture, aquaponics, energy, mining, recreation, and environmental containment markets. Projects include cable wake-board parks in California and Ohio, golf-course ponds in Oregon, greenhouse covers worldwide, a 40-acre irrigation reservoir in the western U.S., frac-tank insulated covers, a coal-mine liner in British Columbia, and custom truck and boat tarps.

The firm emphasizes its 45-year track record, 280-plus years of combined staff experience, and a guarantee of 100% reliability with after-project support. It positions its RPE/RPP materials as stronger, lighter, and more UV-resistant alternatives to traditional HDPE, PVC, or EPDM liners.

Mike later transitioned ownership to Tom and Sarah, while he continued supplying ingredients from his farm.

Today, Barrett runs two facilities: the original Brainerd plant and a 160,000-square-foot facility in Little Falls, Minnesota, opened in 2020 with two additional production lines. The company offers extrusion, freeze-drying, milling, and automated packaging, producing hundreds of formulas for dogs, cats, reptiles, birds, livestock, and zoo animals. Its services span diet formulation, ingredient sourcing, processing, packaging, and global distribution.

Barrett serves emerging and established pet food brands seeking a co-manufacturing partner. Its customer base includes companies in the super-premium kibble and kibble-plus categories, as well as brands requiring specialized diets for exotic and farm animals. The company positions itself as an extension of its partners' teams, handling supply chain logistics and production details.

The business was built on a simple promise: “If we wouldn’t feed it to our own pets, you won’t find it in our products.” Tom and Sarah Barrett emphasize a relationship-based philosophy, personal involvement in each brand, and a “Don’t Say No” mindset that drives innovation. They cite transparency, integrity, and rigorous food-safety standards as key differentiators.

about:
Base Power Company is headquartered in Austin, Texas, and was founded in 2023 by CEO Zach Dell and co‑founder Justin Lopas. Dell, a Texas native, was motivated by Winter Storm Uri’s widespread outages, while Lopas brought manufacturing experience from SpaceX and Anduril. The pair assembled a team with backgrounds in satellite constellations and early‑scale electric‑vehicle production to address rising electricity costs and grid reliability.

The company designs, assembles, and deploys its own 39.2 kWh whole‑home battery system — called Core — and operates as a retail electric provider in Texas and Illinois. Its in‑house capabilities include battery pack assembly, UL‑certified testing, and virtual‑power‑plant grid‑services operation. As of the latest public figures, more than 30,000 homes have been equipped with Base hardware, which is rated for –22 °F to 122 °F, flash flooding, and submersion up to three feet.

Base serves residential homeowners across Texas and Illinois, with a concentration in Oncor territory, and positions its grid‑balancing battery network as a resource for utilities and grid operators. Customer testimonials cite installations in Waxahachie, Cypress, Houston, Arlington, Saginaw, and Pflugerville, and the company counts former NFL player JJ Watt as both an investor and a member.

The founders state they started Base to make electricity affordable and reliable again, offering automatic whole‑home backup at a fraction of traditional generator cost and earning revenue from grid services rather than markup on energy. The goal is to become the first power company customers genuinely love.

Berkwood Farms operates from Des Moines, Iowa, as a farmer-owned coalition of independent family farmers. The company does not disclose a founding year, but its structure reflects generations of family farming, with many participants representing second through fifth generations in animal husbandry. With over 90 farmer-members, Berkwood Farms has grown into one of the largest American suppliers of this specialty pork, achieving national distribution while maintaining its commitment to sustainable farming practices.

The company supplies its pork nationally, serving foodservice, retail, and wholesale channels, though specific customer categories are not detailed in public materials. Its farmer-owned model differentiates it from conventional commodity pork supply chains.

Berkwood Farms was built on the principle that responsible agriculture can be both productive and community-focused. By keeping ownership in the hands of the farmers who raise the animals, the company aims to preserve traditional husbandry methods, ensure animal welfare, and deliver a premium product that reflects the way nature intended.

about:
Berrien Metal Products operates from a 46,000-square-foot facility in Buchanan, Michigan. The company was founded in 1997 and has since focused on manufacturing tanks with integrated plumbing for heat-transfer applications, as well as a range of sheet-metal assemblies, stampings, and tubing-coil assemblies. Ownership details are not publicly disclosed.

The shop runs automated CNC stamping (including a Ton S11 TruPunch 3000 with autoload), a Cincinnati CL-6 CNC laser capable of 1-inch thick material up to 48 by 96 inches, an 8-foot Chicago press brake with CNC gauge, and a machining cell with three mills, a lathe, and multiple drill presses. Core joining processes include soldering, brazing, TIG and MIG welding on steel, stainless steel, aluminum, and copper. Powder coating is outsourced. The company also produces a proprietary foldable podium called the Portable Podium™.

Berrien Metal serves the nuclear industry and has a long track record with government agencies such as the U.S. Army, U.S. Navy, Department of Justice, and Congress, as well as commercial customers including Lockheed Martin, Airgas, and Marathon. Its parts go into military, aerospace, industrial-gas, and energy applications.

The company emphasizes its ISO 9001-certified quality system, lights-out CNC stamping capacity, and a stated commitment to on-time delivery of high-quality metal parts.

old_description: When every second counts, delivering quick and accurate medical results matters. Bluejay Diagnostics is focused on providing products that reduce wait time, improving patient outcomes and potentially saving lives.
about:
Bluejay Diagnostics, Inc. was founded in 2015 in Acton, Massachusetts. The company is publicly traded on the NASDAQ under the ticker BJDX. No founders are named in public materials.

Bluejay is a late-stage, pre-revenue medical device company developing the Symphony™ Suite, a near-patient testing system designed to deliver sample-to-result measurements in approximately 20 minutes. Its first product candidate is an IL-6 test cartridge for sepsis triage, intended for use in hospital and long-term acute care settings. The company is currently conducting the SYMON-II pivotal clinical trial, which completed enrollment of 624 patients in early 2026, and anticipates submitting for FDA approval in 2027.

The Symphony Suite targets clinicians in emergency departments, intensive care units, and long-term acute care facilities who need rapid sepsis diagnosis. By moving testing out of the central laboratory and to the patient bedside, the system aims to accelerate treatment decisions for conditions such as sepsis, where early intervention is critical.

Bluejay states its mission is to enhance patient outcomes through technologies that simplify the diagnostic process and reduce the total cost of care. The self-contained cartridge design eliminates the need for specialized waste handling, and the platform is positioned as a cost-effective alternative to traditional clinical chemistry lab workflows.

Cal-Maine Foods serves retail and foodservice channels nationwide under brands including Eggland's Best, Land O' Lakes, Farmhouse Eggs, Crepini, and Van's Foods. Its customers range from household consumers to foodservice operators and retail chains across the United States.

The company states its purpose is to be the consumer-driven provider of nutritious, affordable, and sustainable eggs and egg-based foods that fit today's lifestyles. It emphasizes a disciplined acquisition strategy — integrating 26 companies since 1989 — and commitments to sustainable operations, strong corporate governance, and community support.

about:
California Fine Wire Co. was founded in June 1961 in Grover Beach, California, when Michael A. Greenelsh started the business with a single wire drawing machine. Over six decades, the company has grown into a multi‑million‑dollar operation supplying specialty wire and ribbon worldwide.

The company manufactures and processes fine and ultra‑fine wire in round and flat profiles, with diameters ranging from 0.0004″ to 0.125″. Core processes include precision drawing, enamel coating (insulating), PTFE and ceramic coating, electroplating, flat‑ribbon rolling, annealing, stranding and twisting, cutting, straightening, and spooling. CFW operates 25 enamel coating machines and maintains an in‑house testing laboratory capable of dimensional measurements to 0.00001″ resolution.

CFW serves highly regulated markets including medical, aerospace, defense, electronics, semiconductor, industrial, and research sectors. Its products are used in implanted cardiac devices, drift chambers, semiconductor interconnects, wire‑bonding assemblies, medical devices, aerospace systems, and high‑temperature industrial sensors. The company works with a broad alloy palette—aluminum, copper, gold, nickel, platinum, refractory metals, stainless steel, thermocouple alloys, and composite‑clad conductors.

Founder Michael A. Greenelsh once said the company’s real specialty is fulfilling customers’ specific needs, a philosophy that has guided CFW for over 60 years. The firm emphasizes tight tolerances, traceable raw materials from approved vendors, and a quality system certified to ISO 9001 with ITAR registration for defense work.

name: Capital Electro Circuits Inc
old_description: exceptional craftsmanship, on-time delivery, and customer-focused solutions
about:
Capital Electro Circuits Inc., based in Gaithersburg, Maryland, has been manufacturing printed circuit boards since 1985. The independently owned company is led by General Manager Raj Jagani and operates a domestic fabrication facility focused on rigid and flexible PCB technologies.

The shop produces rigid, flexible, and rigid‑flex boards with capabilities that include multilayer constructions up to 16 layers, finished thicknesses up to 1.300 inches, copper weights up to 6 oz outer/4 oz inner, and advanced features such as blind/buried vias, edge plating, and castellations. Materials span standard FR‑4 and high‑Tg laminates, polyimides, and a wide range of RF/microwave substrates from Rogers, Arlon, Taconic, and TMM/Teflon families. In‑house services cover CAM with DFM analysis, CNC routing and milling, electrical testing, and a full suite of surface finishes including HASL, ENIG, ENEPIG, immersion tin/silver, and hard gold.

The company serves aerospace and defense (supplying 100 % U.S.-made boards for military and avionics programs), medical and healthcare (precision boards for imaging and diagnostic equipment), telecommunications (high‑frequency circuits for 5G and satellite), automotive and EV (durable boards for electric and autonomous vehicles), and RF/microwave applications. Named customers include Northrop Grumman, BAE Systems, NASA, Lockheed Martin, Honeywell, Sandia National Laboratories, Booz Allen Hamilton, and the U.S. Army.

Capital Electro Circuits positions itself as a specialty fabricator that takes on jobs outside standard PCB lines, often developing custom processes for unique designs. Its stated mission is to support what the customer requires, not only what they ask for, and it maintains a conflict‑minerals sourcing policy with vetted vendors and full CMRT disclosure.

name: Capitol Iron Works
old_description: Based in Rockville, Maryland, Capitol Iron Works specializes in custom ornamental metalwork projects based on unique design ideas, working with ferrous and nonferrous metals, such as stainless steel, aluminum and bronze. The company also works with structural steel and glass. Some of the most common projects include fabrication and installation of architectural railings, stairs, handrails, glass and cable railings, steel fencing, balconies, canopies and automatic gates.
about:
Capitol Iron Works operates from Gaithersburg, Maryland, in the heart of the DC–Maryland–Virginia corridor. The company was founded in August 2014 by Ronald Vargas, who immigrated from Nicaragua in 2004 and learned welding as a helper at Bethesda Iron Works before earning his certification and launching his own shop, initially called Capitol Iron Solutions. Vargas serves as president and co‑owner.

The shop produces custom ornamental and architectural metalwork in ferrous and non‑ferrous metals — stainless steel, aluminum, bronze, structural steel, wrought iron, and glass. Core processes include welding, cutting, shaping, decorative detailing, powder‑coat finishing, and on‑site installation. The facility has expanded from a 1,100‑square‑foot space with a single fabrication bay to a 4,300‑square‑foot plant housing three fabrication units, staffed by 14 employees. Project sizes range from $1,000 residential railings to $500,000 commercial installations, with 2018 revenue projected at $1.5 million.

Capitol Iron Works serves residential, commercial, and government clients across the DMV. Notable government work includes bronze railing fabrication and installation for the Architect of the Capitol at the Rayburn House Office Building. The company also works with architects, contractors, and property owners in cities such as Bethesda, Rockville, Alexandria, and Arlington.

Vargas attributes the firm’s rapid growth to two factors: a loyal, low‑turnover team (only one departure in four years) and a willingness to tackle technically difficult, intricate projects that other shops decline. He emphasizes on‑schedule delivery, direct communication, and a single‑source approach from design through installation.

about:
Capsule Technologies, now operating as Philips Capsule within the Philips Acute Care Informatics portfolio, is headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. The company was acquired by Philips and integrated into its acute care informatics division; its founding year and original founders are not disclosed in public materials.

The company develops vendor‑neutral medical device integration and clinical informatics software. Its platform captures live‑streaming data from over 1,200 medical devices and delivers it to more than 100 downstream systems, including electronic health records, alarm management, and research databases. The portfolio spans medical device integration (Philips Axon, Capsule Neuron, Capsule Vitals Stream, Chart Xpress), a medical device information platform, virtual care management (eCareManager), retrospective analytics (Clinical Insights Manager), clinical surveillance (Capsule Surveillance), and a critical care clinical information system (IntelliSpace Critical Care and Anesthesia).

Customers are hospitals and health systems worldwide. Named references include Hamilton Health Sciences in Canada, CoxHealth in the United States, and Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust in the United Kingdom. The solutions target acute care, perioperative, and virtual care environments.

The company emphasizes a vendor‑neutral, open ecosystem that works with existing infrastructure, deep clinical and operational experience to fit workflows, and a track record of measurable outcomes such as time savings and a seven‑year run of positive Net Promoter Scores.

about:
Captor Corporation was established in 1965 in Tipp City, Ohio, by an engineering-oriented management team that included several experienced veterans. The company built a dedicated manufacturing facility shortly after inception, which has since expanded to a 35,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art plant housing engineering, sales, and production under one roof.

The company designs and manufactures custom EMI filters, capacitors, inductors, coils, cable assemblies, wire harnesses, electromechanical assemblies, and power distribution units. Its in-house capabilities span engineering, custom capacitor winding, coil winding (toroid, bobbin-wound, tube-wound, C-core), cable and harness fabrication, box-build assembly, and environmental testing including altitude, humidity, thermal shock, vibration, and hermetic seal. Captor has produced over 10,000 custom filter designs and focuses on low- to medium-volume production.

Captor serves OEMs in aerospace, defense, military communications, secure communications (including SCIF and TEMPEST applications), medical equipment, telecommunications, radar systems, and missile launching systems.

The company positions itself as a leader in custom EMI filters, stating that its custom solutions are often delivered faster and at lower cost than competitors' off-the-shelf parts, with no added cost for customization. Its mission emphasizes highest-quality EMI filters, customer listening, a safe workplace, continuous improvement, and total customer satisfaction.

old_description: Located in the scenic coastal town of North Kingstown, Rhode Island, in Washington County, this vibrant community of over 27,800 residents is now home to one of Cargill’s newest and most advanced protein processing facilities. Spanning 200,000 square feet, this state-of-the-art slicing and packaging plant specializes in the production of fresh beef, ground beef, pork, and value-added meat products.
about:
Cargill operates one of its newest protein processing facilities in the coastal community of North Kingstown, Rhode Island. The plant, which represents a strategic investment exceeding $120 million, sits on a 200,000-square-foot site at 60 Compass Circle. While the company traces its roots back 160 years, this particular facility is a recent addition to Cargill's North American food network, which comprises roughly 60 processing plants, distribution centers, feed mills, hatcheries, and an innovation center across the United States and Canada.

The North Kingstown plant specializes in slicing and packaging fresh beef, ground beef, pork, and value-added meat products. It is designed to strengthen Cargill's capacity to deliver high-quality protein solutions to retail and foodservice customers throughout the Northeast. Globally, Cargill employs 155,000 people in 70 countries and serves 125 markets across food, agriculture, financial, and industrial sectors.

The facility's output reaches retail and foodservice partners across the Northeast, while the broader company supplies a diverse customer base that includes food manufacturers, agricultural producers, financial services clients, and industrial users. The North Kingstown operation focuses on protein processing for the regional market, complementing Cargill's wider portfolio of food and agricultural ingredients.

Cargill states that its purpose is to nourish the world in a safe, responsible, and sustainable way. The North Kingstown investment underscores a commitment to innovation, food safety, and regional economic development, positioning the plant as a modern hub for protein production in New England.

The company was created at the beginning of 2022 by the owners of Ferry Farms, a Litchfield-based farm, together with a neighboring farmer. They had previously expanded into Ferry Farms Wholesale, distributing snack sticks, jerky, charcuterie, bacon, ground beef, hot dogs, and beer brats, but repeatedly encountered a shortage of USDA-inspected processing and co-packing capacity. That gap led them to establish Carnico as a locally owned and operated facility to serve farms and wholesale businesses across southern Michigan.

The plant provides processing, secondary packaging, private labeling, co-packing, and product development services. It is equipped with smoking capabilities and a state-of-the-art drying and climatic room for producing specialty sausages and cured meats. The facility handles a range of meat products, though specific throughput volumes and headcount are not disclosed.

Carnico’s customer base includes local livestock farms, retail and wholesale food businesses, and its affiliated brand Ferry Farms Wholesale. The company focuses on the southern Michigan region, offering USDA-inspected processing that enables farms to bring branded meat products to market.

The business was founded specifically to overcome the lack of accessible USDA-inspected processing in the area. Its differentiators include on-site smoking, a climate-controlled drying room for cured meats, and integrated flavor and recipe development alongside private-label and co-pack services.

The sawmill uses a mobile hydraulic bandsaw capable of processing logs up to 21 feet long and 32 inches in diameter, with a 26-inch throat capacity. Customers range from property owners with downed trees to contractors in residential, commercial, and industrial construction, as well as woodworkers, furniture makers, agricultural operations, and heavy-equipment transport firms needing blocking and cribbing. The company also purchases logs meeting minimum size requirements (12-inch small-end diameter, eight-foot length) for its own inventory.

The company handcrafts heirloom-quality furniture one piece at a time using solid wood, custom finishes, and customer-specified measurements. Production is organized around three purchasing tiers: in-stock items ready to ship, a line of customizable Farmstead Designs, and fully custom pieces built to a client's exact vision. Most orders ship within two weeks via an in-house white-glove delivery service.

Carolina Farmstead serves residential customers and interior designers seeking durable, made-to-last furnishings for everyday use. Its work has been featured on HGTV's Love It or List It, the PBS series A Chef's Life, and in Our State Magazine, reflecting a focus on pieces that become centerpieces of family gatherings.

The founding mission — creating meaningful employment for the Noble brothers — remains central to the operation. The company emphasizes construction so robust that grown men can stand and jump on the furniture, backs its quality with Better Business Bureau accreditation, and avoids the shortcuts common in mass-market retail.

old_description: An architect emeritus, building contractor, solar installer and real estate developer, Richard founded CSE in 2004. about:
Carolina Solar Energy (CSE) was founded in 2004 in Durham, North Carolina, by Richard Harkrader, an architect emeritus, building contractor, and solar installer. The family-owned business began with a goal to demonstrate that renewable energy legislation could build a solar industry in the state. After years of trial and error, Harkrader completed the first utility-scale solar project in the Southeast at NC State University in 2007. Business partner Gerry Dudzik joined that same year, bringing permitting experience from the cellular tower industry. In 2012, Richard's daughter Carson Harkrader joined after a career at GE Energy, and she assumed leadership in 2018 when both founders retired.

The company develops utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) solar projects across the Southeast and Gulf South, with over 950 MWdc of projects operating or under construction. Its core services include site selection, interconnection applications, state permitting, landowner outreach, community relations, and policy advocacy. The team manages projects from early development through construction, collaborating with municipalities, utilities, and landowners. CSE also operates an intern program and has partnered with organizations like TROSA to provide workforce opportunities.

CSE serves utilities, municipal governments, and private landowners throughout North Carolina, Virginia, Kentucky, and Louisiana. Notable partners include the City of Raleigh, which completed its first major solar development with CSE, and Person County, which hosts three photovoltaic facilities totaling approximately five megawatts. The company focuses on bringing economic development to underserved areas and works with families who have managed land for generations.

CSE distinguishes itself through early-market entry and policy leadership. It was the first solar company to apply for Kentucky state-level permits in March 2020, and its advocacy work has helped shape renewable energy legislation in North Carolina. The firm emphasizes community acceptance, aiming to deliver projects that are welcomed by their host communities.

The owner emphasizes a personal, undivided-attention approach rather than group classes, helping clients interpret sonar returns, adjust settings, and integrate electronics into their fishing strategy.

The customer base consists of recreational and tournament anglers, boat owners, and anyone upgrading or switching brands of marine electronics. Central Kentucky Sonar serves the broader recreational fishing industry across central Kentucky, with clients ranging from weekend hobbyists to competitive bass fishermen seeking to maximize their on-water efficiency.

about:
Certified Parts Corporation (CPC) was founded in 1982 by James Grafft in Edgerton, Wisconsin. The company began with a mission to preserve well-known international and local legacy brands facing extinction. Grafft’s experience at Fox Corporation in Janesville, where he saw the need for continuous parts supply for defunct manufacturers, led him to purchase the service parts division when Fox shut down in 1976. He later acquired the Bridgestone brand on his 26th birthday and established CPC in 1982, acquiring the Arctic Cat snowmobile division from bankruptcy.

Today, CPC operates a 200,000-square-foot factory in Edgerton where it manufactures original service parts, including carburetors and the full line of Comet torque converters and clutches. The company acquires legacy brands—such as TecumsehPower, Comet, Hoffco, Wisconsin Wagon, and vintage recreational vehicle lines—and restarts production of their components. It also manages extensive parts inventories and provides distribution and service support through a worldwide dealer network.

CPC serves OEMs and aftermarket customers in recreational, construction, agricultural, and marine industries. Its brand portfolio includes snowmobile, mini-cycle, watercraft, and outdoor power equipment lines. Concrete examples include supplying Comet clutches to OEM manufacturers across multiple sectors and supporting engines for snowmobiles, mini-cycles, and utility equipment through the Lauson, Snow King, and LCT brands.

The company’s guiding principle is a passion for history and recognizing opportunity in orphaned brands. By acquiring intellectual property, tooling, and inventory, CPC keeps legacy products running and reintroduces historic names to the market, such as the 1895 Lauson engine line.

Chicana Foods is based in Boise, Idaho. The company was founded by first-generation Mexican-American professional photographer Allison Corona with the help of her sisters Claudia and Giovanna and their mother, Gloria. The venture draws on family recipes from Mexico, where the founders' maternal aunts and uncles have operated a salsa business for over two decades.

The company produces salsa macha, a traditional condiment from the Veracruz and Oaxaca regions, using high-quality seeds, nuts, chiles, olive oil, and dried fruit. The recipe was originally developed by an aunt in Mexico and refined in Chicana Foods' Boise kitchen. The operation employs 50 people and runs a production facility in Boise.

Products are sold through a network of independent retailers across Idaho and Utah, including coffee shops such as Flying M Coffee House and Common Ground Coffee, specialty grocers like Idaho Made and Hillfort Farm, farmers markets such as The RealEx Stand, gift shops like Teal Magnolia Gifts, and wine tasting rooms including Indian Creek Winery. The company also sells directly to consumers via its website.

The founders emphasize a family-oriented culture, prioritizing a living wage and safe workplace for all employees. A portion of sales is donated to non-profit organizations such as the Stay-In-School Quinceañera Program, which exposes Latine middle school students to Latine art, literature, and culture.

name: Clearloop Corporation
old_description: Clearloop was founded as a carbon solution by three Tennesseans who want to ensure that the environmental, health, and economic benefits of clean energy reach the communities that need them the most, beginning in our own backyard.
about:
Clearloop Corporation is based in Nashville, Tennessee. Founded by three Tennesseans—Bob Corney, Laura Zapata, and founding chairman Gov. Phil Bredesen—the company began as a carbon solution aimed at delivering the environmental, health, and economic benefits of clean energy to communities that need them most, starting in their own backyard. Clearloop was later acquired by Silicon Ranch, one of the largest independent power producers in the United States, to scale its mission.

Clearloop does not manufacture physical products. Instead, it provides a carbon solutions platform that helps organizations measure, reclaim, and track their carbon footprints by funding the construction of new solar energy facilities. The company’s model directs investment toward solar projects in carbon-intense regions of the U.S. South—including sites in Arcadia, Louisiana; Jackson, Tennessee; Panola County, Mississippi; Paris, Tennessee; and White Pine, Tennessee—where new renewable capacity displaces fossil-fuel generation. The acquisition by Silicon Ranch provides the project development and operational backbone to deliver these projects at scale.

The company works with organizations of all sizes, from global corporations to small businesses and educational institutions. Partners use Clearloop to address Scope 1, 2, and 3 emissions, applying the service to entire product lines, specific SKUs, manufacturing processes, or corporate travel. The platform is designed to be accessible regardless of a company’s sustainability maturity.

Clearloop differentiates itself by building new solar projects rather than purchasing renewable energy credits from existing installations. It focuses on communities traditionally left behind in the energy transition, aiming to maximize both carbon reduction and local economic benefit. The company states that its fee structure—a percentage of the product’s carbon footprint—funds project construction directly, and that every investment is tracked to show tangible clean energy generation over a 40-year project life.

old_description: Complexus Medical is a full-service contract manufacturer of medical devices and healthcare products.
about:
Complexus Medical traces its roots to 1968 when F&F Machine Specialties opened as a small tool-and-die shop in a Mishawaka, Indiana basement. The company rebranded as Complexus Medical and, under the leadership of Michael Behrens, has grown into a full-service contract manufacturer with two modern facilities in Mishawaka and Plymouth, Indiana. A 2013 expansion doubled the Mishawaka headquarters, and a second site was added in 2021 to support increasing demand.

The company provides end-to-end contract manufacturing for medical devices and healthcare products. Its service portfolio covers clean-room assembly, sub-assembly and final assembly, custom kitting and sterile barrier packaging, sterilization coordination (EtO, gamma, and e-beam), supply chain management, regulatory support, and rapid prototyping with tooling development. Complexus handles all welding, finishing, and assembly in-house, enabling control over quality and lead times. The firm reports more than 500 products manufactured and emphasizes FDA-compliant documentation throughout.

Complexus serves medical device OEMs, with a historic focus on the orthopedic device and implant industry. Customers rely on the company for complex instruments that involve multiple components, tight tolerances, and intricate geometry. Typical projects include surgical instrument assemblies, procedure packs, tray configurations, and sterile barrier systems that require validated sterilization processes.

The company positions itself on three differentiators: decades of experience with difficult orthopedic instruments, full in-house control of welding, finishing, and assembly, and a "right-sized" structure that is small enough to manage every project detail yet large enough to deliver at scale. These factors, combined with full-service sterilization coordination and two Indiana locations, form the basis of its value proposition.

Its ITAR-registered, AS9100D- and ISO 9001:2015-certified facility produces military harnesses and molded assemblies deployed in defense equipment worldwide, as well as RF and coaxial cables for commercial and industrial applications.

Compulink emphasizes a performance-based culture built on lean manufacturing, automation, and continuous improvement. Every team member is trained to IPC/WHMA-A-620 workmanship standards, with in-house Level A instructors. The company welcomes customer audits of its quality system and facilities, and maintains documented procedures for traceability, corrective action, and crimp monitoring.

about:
The Valparaiso, Indiana facility began in 1979 as Custom Machining Services, establishing itself as a key domestic source for hydraulic hose crimpers, crimping dies, and related hose equipment. German technology group Continental acquired the plant on November 1, 2017, integrating it into a global automotive supplier network. The site employs approximately 100 people and sits about an hour southeast of Chicago in the community known locally as Valpo. Continental’s North American headquarters are located in Culpeper, Virginia.

The Valparaiso plant specializes in manufacturing hydraulic hose assembly equipment, including crimpers and dies, serving the fluid power distribution market. As part of Continental Corporation, the location operates alongside a broader U.S. manufacturing footprint that includes sites in Clinton, Mississippi; Fairlawn, Ohio; Fort Mill, South Carolina; Marysville, Ohio; Mount Vernon, Illinois; and Sumter, South Carolina. The company’s engineering and technology teams develop radar, sensor, and autonomous driving systems, with recent milestones such as 200 million radar units produced.

Primary customers include hydraulic hose distributors and original equipment manufacturers in the fluid power sector. Through its automotive division—soon to be rebranded as Aumovio—Continental supplies advanced driver-assistance systems to global automakers. Strategic partnerships with Aurora Innovation and NVIDIA aim to deploy driverless trucks at scale, while collaboration with trinamiX on biometric sensing displays earned a CES Innovation Award.

Continental states that its Valparaiso operation distinguishes itself as one of the U.S. producers of hydraulic hose crimping equipment. The corporation emphasizes a mission of advancing safety technologies to get people “SafelyThere,” guided by core values of trust, passion to win, freedom to act, and mutual accountability. The Indiana plant also runs a state-recognized machinist apprenticeship and an assembly technician seal certification program.

name: Control Components, Inc
old_description: Thank you for visiting Control Components! For 35 years our company has specialized in providing a broad range of factory automation and machine safety solution products from leading manufacturers for the Automotive, Industrial, OEM, and Systems Integrator markets.
about:
Control Components, Inc. operates from Pelham, Alabama, where it has spent 35 years supplying factory automation and machine safety products to industrial customers. The company is organized as an Alabama corporation and makes clear that it is not affiliated with the California-based IMI Critical Engineering, which also uses the CCI name. No founding year or individual founders are disclosed in public materials.

The business functions as an authorized distributor rather than a manufacturer. Its line card spans sensors (inductive, photoelectric, ultrasonic, limit switches), machine safety (light curtains, scanners, mats, relays, interlock switches), control panel devices (timers, relays, contactors, circuit breakers, terminal blocks, pushbuttons), industrial communication (Ethernet switches), and process measurement instruments. Staff described as factory-trained assist customers in selecting what the company calls the most cost-effective products for each application.

Primary markets include automotive, general industrial, original equipment manufacturers, and systems integrators. The distributor holds authorized status for brands such as ABB, GE, IDEC, Eaton Cutler-Hammer, Balluff, Pepperl+Fuchs, Schmersal, and dozens of others listed across its catalog.

The company emphasizes technical support and breadth of inventory as its basis for competition, positioning its trained personnel as a resource for matching components to application requirements.

Conway Corp has operated from Conway, Arkansas since 1929, when city leaders signed a charter on May 6 to create the Conway Corporation. The municipal utility was formed to take over the city's electric light plant and, by 1930, its waterworks and sewer plant. It remains a city-owned, nonprofit corporation governed by a local board, with a mission to enhance quality of life through utility and telecommunications services.

The corporation provides electric, water, wastewater, video, internet, voice, and security services to residential and business customers across the Conway area. Its infrastructure includes the Stone Dam Creek Wastewater Treatment Plant, the James H. Crews operate 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, and the company launched one of the earliest broadband cable internet services in the country in 1997.

Customers range from individual households to local businesses and the broader Conway community. The utility serves the city's residential neighborhoods, commercial districts, and a designated Data District where gigabit internet was first rolled out to businesses. It also supports economic development initiatives and education programs as part of its community mandate.

The company states it was founded on a commitment to the community where its employees live and work. Its core values — customer satisfaction, innovation, safety, reliability, responsibility, and community — are framed as the reason it exists, with a focus on delivering safe, affordable, and environmentally sound services while maintaining fiscal stewardship.

old_description: Established in 1995 and based right here in Omaha Nebraska, Corporate Creations specializes in custom screen printing, embroidery and promotional products for the Omaha Metro area including Ralston, Bellevue, Millard, Elkhorn, LaVista and Papillion.
about:
Corporate Creations was founded in 1995 in Omaha, Nebraska, by Wade Lewis while he was an undergraduate at the University of Nebraska at Omaha. Lewis initially launched Greek Creations to serve fraternity and sorority merchandise needs, and the success of that venture led friends and family to request similar custom screen printing, embroidery, and promotional products for their own organizations. Corporate Creations was born from that demand and remains headquartered at 9001 F Street in Omaha, serving the surrounding metro communities including Ralston, Bellevue, Millard, Elkhorn, LaVista, and Papillion.

The company provides custom decoration services centered on screen printing and embroidery, supplemented by a promotional product sourcing program that offers access to over 700,000 items. In-house capabilities include graphic design, digitizing for embroidery, art proofing with a 48-hour turnaround, and rush production options. Orders are produced at their Omaha facility with typical lead times of 10 business days after art approval. Minimum order quantities are set at six pieces for embroidery, 12 pieces for screen printing, and 100 pieces for most promotional products, though embroidery reorders carry no minimum.

Corporate Creations serves a broad base of local clients: businesses, clubs, sports teams, churches, charities, schools, universities, and non‑profit organizations throughout the Omaha metro area. The company also continues to support Greek‑life organizations through its affiliated brand Greek Creations. Customers range from small community groups to larger corporate accounts, all receiving the same design‑to‑delivery workflow.

The business was started to simplify and improve the way groups purchased custom merchandise, and that mission persists in a focus on low minimums, transparent pricing, and a collaborative art process that includes two free revisions. The company highlights its award‑winning design team and its recognition as Omaha Magazine’s Best of Omaha Custom T‑Shirt Store winner from 2021 through 2025 as evidence of its service quality.

CWI specializes in custom architectural millwork, handling engineering, fabrication, and installation of reception areas, wall paneling (including exotic and blueprint‑matched veneers and opaque lacquer finishes), doors and sidelights, and pantry/cafe/servery units. The shop produces thousands of square feet of paneling and thousands of door systems annually, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

The company serves the commercial construction industry, supplying corporate offices, institutional projects, and other interior build‑outs where high‑quality millwork is required. CWI differentiates itself through the “Andersen Way” — a philosophy built on relationships, integrity, agility, teamwork, and efficiency — and through its participation in the Architectural Woodwork Institute’s Quality Certification Program (QCP), which validates adherence to stringent design and manufacturing standards.

name: Craftco
old_description: Started as a job shop in 1981 by founders Billy and Marva Craft, Craftco has grown to become a nationwide leader in welding, manufacturing, materials handling, assembly and processing. We operate out of our 25,000-square-foot facility right here in Sheridan, Wyoming, and we take pride in building relationships and solving problems through customer service. Read about our services, capabilities, and even some of the products we build.
about:
Craftco began in 1981 as a one-person welding shop in Sheridan, Wyoming, founded by Billy and Marva Craft. The company remains a family-run business that has expanded from welding into a full-service manufacturing operation.

Today Craftco provides welding and fabrication (including heavy plate forming, waterjet cutting, and certified structural welding), precision CNC machining (turning and milling to tight tolerances), materials processing (raw stock management, precision sawing), coating and assembly (multi-layer protective coatings, sub-assembly, turnkey builds), and engineering and design support (DFM analysis). All services operate under one roof at the 25,000-square-foot facility, serving projects ranging from one-off components to ongoing production partnerships.

The company serves customers nationwide across mining, firearms manufacturing, fossil fuel extraction, robotics, commercial and residential construction, structural building, and oil and gas. A notable international project in 2012 delivered wear liner plates to the Antofagasta mine in Chile. Craftco also partners with large commercial contractors and agricultural equipment builders throughout the Rocky Mountain region and beyond.

Craftco positions itself as more than a job shop, emphasizing engineering-driven problem solving and long-term partnerships. Its stated mission focuses on quality, value, professionalism, integrity, safety, teamwork, and respect, guided by a “Code of the West” ethos. The firm invests in new technology through industry conferences such as FabTech and maintains a fleet of vehicles for on-site service.

name: Creative Composites Group, Augusta Molding Division
old_description: Creative Composites Group can help you advance your infrastructure projects beyond the limitations of traditional materials. We are the largest manufacturer of structural composites in the U.S. with innovative products across multiple industries.
about:
Creative Composites Group’s Augusta Molding Division operates from Augusta, Maine, as part of the Kenway Composites business unit. The division belongs to Creative Composites Group (CCG), a U.S.-based collection of composite manufacturers owned by Hill & Smith Holdings PLC, a UK-listed engineering group with divisions in engineered solutions, roads & security, and galvanizing services. CCG was formed to combine the expertise of several established composite companies, though a specific founding year for the Augusta operation is not publicly stated.

The division produces fiber-reinforced polymer (FRP) structural components and systems, offering design-build, structural fabrication, manufacturing, and engineering services. Its capabilities extend to industrial field services, specialized coatings, FRP repair and maintenance, tank and tower installation, lining, and pulp mill repair. The group emphasizes turnkey solutions from concept through installation, leveraging advanced composite manufacturing processes across its network of facilities.

Customers span telecommunications and data centers, energy generation and distribution, marine, rail, housing, pulp and paper, water and wastewater treatment, and chemical storage. The company cites telecom and data centers as a served industry, while its parent group’s portfolio includes infrastructure markets such as energy, marine, and rail.

CCG positions itself as the largest manufacturer of structural composites in the United States, differentiating through vertical integration of design, engineering, and manufacturing across multiple specialized brands. The organization highlights over 60 years of collective field service experience and an integrated model that combines the capabilities of its member companies to deliver corrosion-resistant, lightweight, and long-lasting composite solutions.
